recent_posts.title: The gaps in South Africa’s digital ID plan
recent_posts.summary: South Africa's newly published draft digital identity regulations have been welcomed by industry experts as a starting point, but several critical gaps have been identified. Concerns include reliance on 2D selfie liveness checks that are vulnerable to deepfake attacks, with experts recommending multi-factor authentication using NFC, PINs, or fingerprint scans. The draft focuses heavily on the MyMzansi app as the sole wallet, contrasting with international trends allowing multiple certified wallets like Apple Wallet or Google Wallet. The regulations also say little about verifiers — banks, retailers, and government departments that need to read credentials — and leave open questions about multi-device support, lost phone recovery, offline use, and fraud signal collection. Positives include a data minimisation principle aligned with POPIA, allowing selective disclosure such as age verification without revealing full ID details. Public commentary is open until 6 June.

recent_posts.title: South Africa’s TikTok election is coming
recent_posts.summary: South Africa's November 2026 municipal elections face a significant disinformation threat that existing broadcast regulations from Icasa are ill-equipped to address. The rules apply only to traditional broadcasters like SABC and eMedia, leaving TikTok, X, YouTube, and Instagram entirely unregulated. Drawing on international examples — a deepfake audio clip that may have swung Slovakia's 2023 election, TikTok manipulation that caused Romania to annul its 2024 presidential vote, and Iranian AI-generated Lego animations racking up millions of views — the piece argues South Africa is vulnerable. Local precedents include Bell Pottinger's bot-driven 'white monopoly capital' campaign and a fake Trump voice endorsement of the MK Party. With AI voice cloning now essentially free, the IEC's cooperation agreement with Meta, TikTok, and Google (notably excluding X) is insufficient without enforceable synthetic content disclosure rules.

recent_posts.title: Hexion deploys 30 petabyte sovereign data archive in South Africa
recent_posts.summary: Hexion Data Storage has deployed a 30 petabyte deep archive storage platform in South Africa, targeting enterprises that need local data sovereignty, predictable pricing, and cyber resilience. The platform avoids egress and retrieval fees, operates on a private 'dark' network isolated from the public internet, and offers immutable storage to guard against ransomware. It is aimed at regulated sectors like financial services, healthcare, and government that face compliance pressures around offshore data residency.

recent_posts.title: Altron’s FY26 earnings seen firmer as platforms power growth
recent_posts.summary: Altron has updated its FY26 earnings guidance, with headline earnings per share from continuing operations expected to rise 31-37% to between R2.33 and R2.43. At group level, Heps is projected to climb 68-74%, well above the 50% growth flagged in February. The Platforms segment — comprising Netstar, Altron FinTech, and Altron HealthTech — drives roughly 90% of Ebitda despite contributing only 45% of revenue. Annuity revenue exceeded 65% of total group revenue, underpinning stronger cash flow. FY26 marks the end of Altron's three-year accelerated growth phase, with a capital markets day planned for June and full results due 25 May.

recent_posts.title: Datatec reports 51-59% jump in headline earnings per share for FY2026
recent_posts.summary: JSE-listed ICT group Datatec has reported a sharp jump in earnings for its 2026 financial year, with headline earnings per share expected to rise 51-59% to between 38.5 and 40.5 US cents. The strong performance was driven by its Westcon International cybersecurity and networking distribution business and Logicalis International IT solutions arm. Datatec's share price rose 1.5% on the news, with shares up nearly 25% over the past year, giving the group a market valuation of R17.2-billion. Full 2026 financial results are expected on 26 May 2026.

recent_posts.title: How AI automation threatens junior developer career pathways in South Africa
recent_posts.summary: AI tools like GitHub Copilot and Amazon CodeWhisperer are automating the routine tasks that traditionally served as training grounds for junior developers. In South Africa, where the tech sector is a key driver of social mobility and youth employment, this shift risks creating a 'missing middle' — a generation of engineers who advance without developing foundational problem-solving skills. The piece outlines four priorities to address this: redesigning early-career pathways into AI-enabled apprenticeships, investing in structured mentorship, adopting responsible AI integration policies, and updating national digital skills frameworks to reflect AI-augmented development realities.

recent_posts.title: SpaceX IPO filing reveals unprecedented governance terms giving Musk unchecked control
recent_posts.summary: SpaceX's upcoming IPO filing reveals governance terms that give Elon Musk near-total control over the company. Through a dual-class share structure, Musk will hold 83.8% of voting power while owning 42.5% of equity. The bylaws eliminate class-action lawsuits, mandate private arbitration, restrict shareholder proposals, and incorporate Texas corporate law — all combining to strip investors of typical protections. Despite these restrictions, the IPO is expected to be the largest in history, targeting a $1.75 trillion valuation and $75 billion in proceeds, with many portfolio managers feeling compelled to buy in regardless. Governance experts warn this could set a precedent for other high-profile founder-led IPOs, including Anthropic and OpenAI.

recent_posts.title: Yoco brings in external CEO from European fintech sector
recent_posts.summary: South African payments fintech Yoco has appointed Carsten Höltkemeyer as CEO, effective 1 June 2026. Höltkemeyer comes from European banking and fintech, most recently serving as CEO of Berlin-based Solaris. He replaces founding CEO Katlego Maphai, who stepped down in September 2025. Co-founders Bradley Wattrus and Lungisa Matshoba, who served as interim co-CEOs, will transition to CFO and chief product and technology officer roles respectively. Yoco now serves over 200,000 merchants, processes 30 million card taps annually, and plans to leverage AI and integrated software in its second decade to help independent businesses compete against banks and legacy providers.

recent_posts.title: South Africa’s patching problem is about to get worse
recent_posts.summary: South African organisations already struggle with timely patch management, and the rapid enterprise adoption of AI agents is set to worsen the problem. Zaheer Ebrahim of TrendAI warns that if organisations can't patch conventional systems promptly, they'll be even less equipped to patch AI agents running in their environments. A TrendAI simulation demonstrated how AI agents can be manipulated via hidden instructions in emails — requiring no malware and no user interaction. The Auditor-General's 2024/2025 report found 45 of 70 government entities had notable cybersecurity weaknesses, including absent vulnerability management tools. With no chief AI officer at most large enterprises, accountability for AI-related breaches falls to CIOs or CISOs who may lack full visibility. The recommended fix is straightforward: get the security basics right before deploying AI agents at scale.

recent_posts.title: AI is rewriting the threat playbook
recent_posts.summary: South Africa's draft National AI Policy was withdrawn after AI-generated fictitious citations were found in the document, highlighting the risks of ungoverned AI. A Palo Alto Networks regional director argues this policy setback doesn't change the underlying cybersecurity threat reality: frontier AI models are accelerating vulnerability discovery dramatically, with one exercise achieving a year's worth of findings in under three weeks. Attackers are targeting AI tools and software supply chains, and tasks that once took days will soon take minutes. Organizations are urged to invest in fast, AI-driven security operations regardless of the policy rewrite timeline.
